The maximum energy of emitted photoelectrons is 2 eV. When photons of energy 6 eV are incident on C, no photoelectrons will reach the anode A, if the stopping potential of A relative to C is A + 3 V B +4 V C -1 V D -3 V Check Answer 2 NEET 2016 Phase 1 MCQ (Single Correct Answer) +4 -1 English Hindi An electron of mass m and a photon have same energy E. The ratio of de-Broglie wavelengths associated with them is A c{( {2mE} \)^{{1 \over 2}}} B {1 \over c}{( {{{2m} \over E}} \)^{{1 \over 2}}} C {1 \over c}{( {{E \over {2m}}} \)^{{1 \over 2}}} D {( {{E \over {2m}}} \)^{{1 \over 2}}} Check Answer 3 NEET 2016 Phase 1 MCQ (Single Correct Answer) +4 -1 English Hindi When a metallic surface is illuminated with radiation of wavelength \lambda , the stopping potential is V.
